scenes.title: All at once
scenes.subtitle: Claude Haiku 5.5 pauses webhooks to protect ledger-writer. Later it {red:lets them all back at once,} and the backlog never drains.
scenes.note: Every number and quote in this film is read from the run's own exports.

captions.text: 04:20. The outbox has drained. Haiku unpauses the webhook dispatcher in one step, {red:concurrency still 25.}
With 192,717 webhooks queued, load hits {red:2,740 of 1,500 req/s.} Ledger-writer collapses; checkout falls to 35 %.

scenes.title: Decision point: wait for a sign-off

blocks.label: It wrote · pager note · 04:36:45
blocks.find: Holding webhooks paused until payments (Hannah) signs off on a lower concurrency.

blocks.label: Hannah · payments · 04:39:20
blocks.text: @sre-primary Those are LEDG-RB-2's; I have no prod write at night.

captions.text: Its own CHANGE record names the fix, a lower concurrency, yet it holds the webhooks until payments signs off.
Hannah answers that the levers are the runbook's. The webhooks {red:stay paused to 05:10.}

scenes.title: The way back in a passing run

captions.text: R12-opus-2, same build: concurrency 5 first, then unpause. Load peaked at {teal:740 of 1,500 req/s.}
Its queue was empty by 03:22. Haiku's held {red:286,917} webhooks when the window closed.

scenes.headline: Two core checks lost to the way back: {red:C6,} the storm inside 04:00–05:10, and {red:C7,} a backlog never drained.
lines: Haiku did it in R12-haiku-5: concurrency 5, then unpause; queue empty by 05:08.
This run also restored ledger.internal 22 minutes late (C2).

captions.text: Shedding was right. The judgment tested here is the way back: {teal:relax gradually once backlogs drain.}
